title: Dynamic epoch-based quota allocator and commit-window enforcement
creator: Ava Chen
description: Introduce an epoch-based quota allocator that unifies daily/monthly anchoring and rolling-window semantics into a single, efficient commit window model. This change targets correctness of usage accounting across hosted and reserved capacity products, reduces burst reconciliation complexity, and enables sub-second enforcement for API rate limiting. The allocator will maintain compact epoch counters per tenant+route, support configurable commit windows (aligned, rolling, and hybrid), and allow zero-downtime migration with backward-compatible read/write paths.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Quota consumption is recorded in epoched counters and reconciles to the same per-tenant totals as the legacy system within +/- 0.01% for a representative workload
2) Rolling-window semantics (e.g., 30-minute sliding window) can be expressed and enforced via epoch spans without per-request full history scans
3) Reserved capacity commitments are enforced against epoched quotas with correct priority (reserved first, shared pool second), and no customer sees unexpected token throttles during migration
4) API compatibility: existing quota APIs (GET /quota, POST /consume) work unchanged during rollout; new endpoints for diagnostic introspection are available behind a feature flag
5) Performance: median quota-check latency <= 2ms additional overhead at P95 tail under production concurrency compared to baseline
design_decisions: Use fixed-length epoch buckets (configurable granularity: 1m, 5m, 1h) stored in Redis for hot counters and periodically persisted to primary metering store (Postgres) for long-term accounting
Model rolling windows as a sum across the N most-recent epochs (sliding-sum) to avoid per-request scanning of event logs
Reserved capacity tracked as separate quota-class; allocator first decrements reserved epoch counters, then falls back to shared epoch counters with optional throttling policy
Adopt optimistic write-through strategy: write to Redis (fast path) and enqueue durable write to metering pipeline. On Redis miss fallback to metering store read-repair
Provide read-after-write guarantees per request using a local in-process cache for the request lifecycle to ensure idempotency in retries
implementation_notes: Schema: add epochs table in Postgres: (tenant_id, route, epoch_start_iso, epoch_granularity, consumed_units) — note: store as text/date/number columns; migrations will backfill from existing usage_events
Redis layout: key pattern quota:epoch:{tenant}:{route}:{granularity}:{epoch_start} -> integer consumed. Use HINCRBY for atomic increments during consume path
API: keep existing quota endpoints; add ?version=epoch to query epoched breakdown. New internal endpoint POST /internal/quota/commit to atomically flush an epoch batch to Postgres
Instrumentation: emit 'quota.epoch.consume' histograms and 'quota.reconcile.delta' gauges. Tag by tenant, environment, and reserved=true/false
Concurrency: use short TTL locks (50ms) only for rare cross-process reconciliation; main path must be lock-free to meet tail latency goals
Backfill: daily job to convert last 90 days of usage_events into epoched aggregates. Backfill runs in low-traffic windows and can be paused per-tenant
Fallbacks: if Redis unavailable, proxy consumes to a degraded synchronous path that writes directly to Postgres with rate-limiters to protect DB
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): implement epoch allocator behind feature flag; route 5 internal test tenants and internal tooling (dev/staging) to new path. Monitor correctness metrics and latency for 72h
Phase 2 (opt-in customers): enable for selected small external tenants with non-critical SLAs and run comparative accounting for 7 days
Phase 3 (mixed): enable for 20% of production traffic using header-based routing and run reconciliation job nightly. Support automated rollback via feature flag
Phase 4 (full): flip feature flag for all tenants, retire legacy rolling-window aggregator after 14-day observation and final reconciliation
Migration: run backfill job in parallel to populate historical epochs; once parity achieved, switch read path to epoched store for downstream billing exports
testing_plan: Unit tests for epoch summation logic and reserved-first decrement semantics
Integration harness that replays production trace (1h sample) against both legacy and epoch allocator and asserts totals match within tolerance
Chaos test: simulate Redis partitions and ensure fallback path preserves correctness and emits alerts
Load test: synthetic traffic to validate P95 latency budget at target QPS and verify no DB saturation during fallback
E2E billing validation: run sample invoices using epoched exports and verify numbers against current billing pipeline for 30 customers
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: Quota-epoch ingestion rate, redis hit rate, reconcile delta distribution, per-tenant reserved vs shared consumption
Alerts: reconcile.delta > 0.5% across production tenants for >1h, redis error rate > 0.5% for 10m, direct-postgres-fallback > 1% of consumes
SLOs: consumer-facing quota-check added latency P95 < 10ms, correctness regression < 0.1% from baseline
Runbooks: link to incident runbook for "epoch-allocator divergence" and steps to toggle feature-flag and backfill
